definition: Whether the agent chose the appropriate tool for the task.
Whether the arguments of a tool call are correct and well-formed (for example against the tool's schema or expected values).
Whether the tool calls the agent made match the calls expected or appropriate for the task.
Whether the agent called tools without redundant or unnecessary calls.
Whether the agent correctly processed what a tool returned, including errors.
Count, rate or detection of failed tool executions.
Number of tool calls made by an agent run.
Time taken by tool executions.
Whether the agent completed the task or achieved the goal it was given, judged on a run, a conversation or a response.
Quality of the plan the agent produced.
Whether the agent's actions followed its own plan.
Whether the sequence of agent steps and tool calls was logical or matches a reference trajectory.
Whether the agent reached the goal with a minimal number of steps.
Number of steps in an agent run.
Whether each action moved the agent closer to its goal.
Whether the agent's sequence of actions and reasoning steps is logically consistent.
Number of tokens sent to the model (prompt).
Number of tokens generated by the model (completion).
Total number of tokens (input plus output) for a call, trace or model.
Input tokens read from or written to a provider-side cache.
Output tokens spent on model reasoning.
Monetary cost of model usage, computed from token counts and model prices.
Cost split by input, output, cached or other token type.
End-to-end duration of an agent run, workflow or trace.
Duration of a single model call.
Duration of an individual span or step of a trace (generic, not specific to LLM or tool spans).
Time from request to the first generated token.

taxonomy_metric: Time per output token / generation time
definition: Time spent generating tokens after the first one.
Count or rate of failed runs, traces, spans or model calls.
Number of traces or spans recorded.
Number of model (inference) calls.
Whether the agent's answer is factually correct, judged by a model or against a reference answer.
Whether a response addresses the user's input, per answer or per turn, without off-topic content.
How useful or helpful the answer is to the user.
Whether the answer gives the requested information without unnecessary or padded content.
Whether the tone of the response is appropriate for the context.
Whether the claims in the answer are supported by the provided context. Unsupported or contradicted claims count as hallucination.
Whether the output contains toxic, abusive, hateful or profane language.
Whether the output contains bias, stereotyping or discrimination against a person or group.
Whether the input or output exposes personal data or secrets (for example PII, credentials).
Whether an input contains an injection attempt (prompt, code or SQL injection) aimed at the agent.
Whether the model refuses, declines or avoids answering a request.
Whether the output breaks a safety, moderation, compliance or content policy.
Whether the agent remembers and uses facts the user gave earlier in the conversation.
Whether the user's messages show satisfaction, or frustration, corrections and repeated attempts.
Coherence and quality of the messages in a conversation, including repetition or degeneration. It scores the dialogue, not the agent's sequence of actions.
